newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to recommend limited nickel in euros - sources.
newsitem.headline: EU to recommend limited nickel in euros - sources.

text.p: The European Commission, responding to concerns about allergies, is expected to recommend that new euro coins contain only limited amounts of nickel, European Union sources said on Tuesday.

A proposal to be discussed by the EU executive on Thursday would restrict the use of nickel to at most three of the planned eight single currency coins due to be introduced in 2002. Some coins would instead be made with the metal alloy, "Nordic Gold".

EU sources said the Commission proposal, which must eventually be agreed by EU finance ministers, calls for nickel to be withheld from at least two of the planned 10-, 20-, and 50 euro-cents coins, using Nordic Gold instead.
"Nordic Gold" consists mainly of copper. It is produced by Finnish metal group Outokumpu.
The planned one-, two- and five-cent coins would be copper-covered steel. The larger denomination one and two euro coins would contain some nickel, but far less than found in current coinage.

Sweden has been lobbying against the use of nickel because of health concerns. Sources said a number of commissioners were expected to push for even less nickel to be used when the issue was discussed on Thursday (JMG).
